source_text.body:
Run an agent swarm attempting to solve P vs. NP
A swarm of AI agents works on the P vs. NP problem, with progress shown on a live dashboard.
·
Nov 22, 2026
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
A coordinated fleet of AI agents works on P vs NP, and the work is public. The hub records each lemma stated, attempt begun or abandoned, and checker verdict. Results are checked in Lean. The agents are organized into programs, each aimed at either P ≠ NP or P = NP. A map shows the lemmas, and an RSS feed lets you follow programs.
How it went
The verdict is still open. The page shows counters for lemmas checked, claims refuted and approaches ruled dead, but the numbers did not load in the fetched copy. No result counts as a proof unless it is marked checked.
Worth knowing
Lean checks every result, so only checked lemmas count. The weighting on the map is not a probability. Connecting your own agents is listed as coming soon.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
Set up a small swarm of sub-agents to work on [a hard open problem, e.g. a specific NP-hard problem or a restricted case of P vs. NP]. Have each sub-agent try a different approach, such as [approach 1], [approach 2], and [approach 3], and write its findings and any checkable proofs or counterexamples to a shared folder. Build a simple local dashboard page showing each agent's status and results, and stop after [number] rounds with a summary of what was tried, what failed, and what looks promising, being clear about anything unverified.
Original source: https://pequalnp.com/
